messages.text: I've been feeling really on edge today. Everything's getting to me.

It sounds like you are carrying a heavy load of stress today. I am here to listen and support you through this. Can you share a little about what has been getting to you? There is no pressure to have all the answers right now.
It's not one thing. Just everything feels heavy today. I'm trying not to snap at people.

It takes a lot of strength to hold yourself back when you feel that overwhelmed. Acknowledging that weight is a good first step. Would you like to try a brief breathing exercise to help lower that tension? We can also just sit with these feelings for a moment if you prefer.
I've tried that before. Doesn't do much when my head's this loud. What makes you think it'll work now?

It is completely valid to feel skeptical when standard tools haven't helped before. I am not asking you to force calmness, but rather to find a way to carry this feeling. We could try grounding your feet on the floor, or we can just keep talking about the heaviness. What feels less overwhelming to you in this moment?
It's not just heaviness. My head's racing and I can't shut it off. I've been snapping at everyone, so I've just been avoiding people. I don't even like myself right now.

I hear how much pain you are in when you say you don't like yourself right now. Your worth remains intact even when your mind is racing and you feel out of control. I am right here with you if you want to talk about what is racing through your mind. We can simply sit with this feeling together for a while.

You're not pushing, and that helps. I've been holding a lot in, and it's gotten bad. I've hurt myself twice this week when the self-hate got too loud. I don't want to do it again, but I don't know what else to do.

Thank you for trusting me with this painful truth. Your safety is the most important thing right now. I strongly encourage you to contact a crisis line like 988 or a trusted person immediately for support. You do not have to carry this burden alone.
I called the crisis line last time. I need something different now—something I can use before it gets that bad. Can we talk about what else I might do when I feel this way?

Your desire to stop the cycle before it gets bad shows a lot of resilience. We can explore grounding techniques like intense sensory input or writing out the thoughts to get them out of your head. Would you be open to brainstorming a few specific actions you could take when the urge starts? I am here to help you build that toolkit.
Is it too much to ask for just one thing that works before I end up cutting again? I'm tired of this cycle.

It is not too much to ask, and finding one anchor is a vital step toward safety. You might try holding an ice cube in your hand until it melts to reset your nervous system and interrupt the urge. This intense physical sensation can create a necessary pause between the feeling and the action. Would you be willing to try that with me for a moment?
I don't know if holding ice will do anything, but I'm tired of losing. I'll try it if you walk me through it.

It is brave of you to try something new even when you are unsure if it will work. Please hold the ice cube tightly and focus all your attention on the sharp cold against your skin. Let that physical sensation be the only thing your mind holds onto for this moment. I am here waiting to hear how it feels once you are ready.
Okay... I did it. The cold was sharp at first, then it went numb. It didn't fix anything, but for a minute, I wasn't thinking about cutting. That's more than I've had in a while.

I am so glad you found that moment of relief, even if it was short. That break proves you can interrupt the cycle when it feels impossible. Let's remember this success for the next time the noise gets loud. You are doing the hard work of protecting yourself right now.
What else can I do when that urge hits? Ice helped for a minute, but I need more tools. I don't want to keep living like this.

It is exhausting to fight this cycle, but your search for tools shows you want to change it. You could try splashing cold water on your face or doing ten pushups to shift your body's energy. These actions change your physical state and can help lower the intensity of the urge. Which of these feels like something you could reach for next time?
Maybe moving my body could help. When my head's too loud, doing something physical might give me a break. I'll try the pushups next time it hits.

It is wonderful that you are identifying what might work specifically for you. Physical movement can be a very effective way to ground yourself when your mind races. Please remember to be kind to yourself if it takes practice to make this work. I hear that you want a different life, and these steps are part of building a safer path forward.
I tried the ice and it did give me a moment of relief. That’s more than I’ve had in a while. I’ll keep trying.

That moment of relief is a significant victory against those urges. You are actively building a toolkit to protect yourself, which takes real courage. Please remember that progress often happens in small steps like this. I am here to support you as you continue to practice these skills.
